classification.difficultyReason: Combines equal-side properties, equilateral and isosceles triangles, and several angle relationships in composite figures.

content.prompt: Find the value of $x$ in these diagrams.

spec.description: Unshaded house-shaped pentagon with five matching single equality ticks, two bottom right-angle squares, and red dashed segments from the roof apex to both bottom corners. The angle between the dashed segments is labelled x degrees.
spec.mathematics: Both upright sides are perpendicular to the base and equal to it. Their upper endpoints are separated by the base length, so the equal roof edges form an equilateral triangle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source unknown x is visible; no numerical answer or added construction is printed.

answer.short: $x=30^{\circ}$. Join the upper ends of the vertical sides to form an equilateral roof triangle.
answer.worked:
Join the upper ends of the vertical sides. The lower quadrilateral is a square, so the new segment equals each roof edge. The roof triangle is therefore equilateral, with each angle $60^{\circ}$.

Each angle where a vertical side meets a roof edge is $90^{\circ}+60^{\circ}=150^{\circ}$. Each side triangle formed by a red dashed segment is isosceles, since its two outer edges are equal. Its two base angles are
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{base angle}&=\frac{180^{\circ}-150^{\circ}}{2}\\
&=15^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$
The two dashed segments split the roof apex angle into $15^{\circ}$, $x$ and $15^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{aligned}
x+15^{\circ}+15^{\circ}&=60^{\circ}\\
x&=30^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Unshaded square-shaped outer quadrilateral. All four sides and both solid segments from the bottom corners to the interior apex have matching single ticks. Red dashed segments join the interior apex to both top corners. Their upper angle is labelled x degrees. No right-angle markers are added.
spec.mathematics: The lower triangle is equilateral and the equal outer sides establish a rhombus. Its adjacent bottom angles are supplementary. The two side triangles are isosceles, and their angles at the interior apex total 150 degrees. Angles around that apex give x = 150 degrees without requiring a square designation.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source unknown x is visible; no supplied numerical answer or inferred right-angle markers are printed.

answer.short: $x=150^{\circ}$. Use supplementary adjacent angles of the rhombus and the equal base angles of the two side triangles.
answer.worked:
The outer quadrilateral is a rhombus because its four sides are equal. The lower triangle is equilateral because its three sides are equal, so each of its angles is $60^{\circ}$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be the angles between an outer side and a solid interior segment at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners. Adjacent angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so
$$\begin{aligned}
(a+60^{\circ})+(b+60^{\circ})&=180^{\circ}\\
a+b&=60^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$
Each side triangle is isosceles, since its outer side and solid interior segment are equal. Their angles at the interior apex therefore total
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{180^{\circ}-a}{2}+\frac{180^{\circ}-b}{2}&=\frac{360^{\circ}-(a+b)}{2}\\
&=150^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$
Using the angles around the interior apex,
$$\begin{aligned}
x+150^{\circ}+60^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\
x&=150^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$
